title: SpellSheetApi
description: Bundle of the IPC/API payload types used by Studio and MCP tools.

Flow.title: Flow
Flow.description: A flow: the unit that AI clients, Studio and the Runtime share.

$schema.description: Optional JSON Schema reference for editors. Ignored by SpellSheet.

schemaVersion.description: Version of the flow file format.

requires.description:
Plugins the steps need, with the versions they were written for:
`{ "plugin:kintone": "^0.3.1" }`. Kept up to date by Core when steps
are added or removed, so authors normally leave it alone.

revision.description:
Monotonic revision, incremented by every committed edit. Used for
optimistic concurrency between Studio, MCP clients and the CLI.

parts.description:
Named screen parts (a button, a field…): a node's `target` can be
`{ "part": "<name>" }` instead of the whole target, so a part that
changes is fixed in one place. Keys are like variable names.

settings.description: Flow-wide defaults for error handling, timeouts and retries.

FlowId.description: Identifier of a flow. Also used as its file name in the store.

name.description:
Identifier used in expressions: letters of any script (orderNo, 受注番号),
digits and `_`, not starting with a digit.

secret.description: Secret values are masked in logs, events and run records.

personal.description:
Personal data (names, addresses, mail, rows of customers…): masked
like a secret in logs, events, run records, errors and notifications,
and left out of exported bundles and saved test cases. Unlike a
secret it may have a default and be passed in as plain text.

format.description:
What a `string` input holds, so the run window can offer the right
field (a file picker, a calendar). Runs do not check it.

choices.description:
The only values an input takes: the run window shows a list to pick
from. Each one must match `type`.

oneOf.description: Supplied by the caller when the run starts.
Returned to the caller when the run finishes.
Both supplied and returned.
The full path of an existing file.
The full path of a folder.
A day, `YYYY-MM-DD`.
A month, `YYYY-MM`.

Part.description: A named screen part: what a node finds on screen, kept in one place.

label.description: What people call it (保存ボタン). The key is for nodes and AI.

app.description: The kind of node that can use it.

target.description:
The target, exactly as the nodes of `app` take it. Left out (null)
when the author could not see the screen (an AI in a chat window):
a person picks it in Studio, and until then the nodes that use the
part do not validate (`PART_NOT_PICKED`).

Step.description: A single step. Control-flow and action steps share this shape.

id.description: Stable unique ID. Omit when adding a step; Core assigns one.

name.description: Display label (Japanese is fine). Purely informational.

params.description:
Type-specific parameters, validated against the step type's schema.
String values may contain `{{ expression }}` templates.

blocks.description: Child step lists of control-flow steps, keyed by block name.

disabled.description: Disabled steps are skipped by the Runtime but kept in the flow.

onError.description: What to do when the step still fails after retries.

saveAs.description: Variable that receives the step's output value.

meta.description:
Free-form metadata (Studio layout hints, AI provenance such as the UI
element a selector was derived from). Never interpreted by the Runtime.

StepId.description: Identifier of a step. Unique within a flow and stable across edits.

maxAttempts.description: Total attempts including the first one (1 = no retry).

backoffMultiplier.description: Multiplier applied to the delay after each failed attempt.

oneOf.description: Stop the run (or hand control to the enclosing `control.try`).
Record the error in `lastError` and continue with the next step.

defaultTimeoutMs.description: Default per-step timeout in milliseconds (30 s when omitted).

keepWork.description:
Leave the files in the flow's `work/` folder when a run starts.
By default a run starts with `work/` emptied.

inputs.description:
Input variables (`input` and `inOut`), in declared order: what a
`flow.call` to it can pass in.

outputs.description: Output variables (`output` and `inOut`): what a call can receive.

secrets.description:
Secrets its steps refer to by name: the secrets page shows where
each one is used.

oneOf.description: Inserts a step (and its children). Missing IDs are generated.
Removes a step and all of its children.
Adds or replaces (by name) a variable declaration.

index.description: Position in the variable list when adding; ignored when replacing.

oneOf.description:
Adds or replaces (by name) a named screen part. Nodes use it as
`"target": { "part": "<name>" }`.
Replaces the whole step tree (bulk edits by AI, imports).

Position.description: Where a step lives (or should be inserted).

parentId.description: Parent control-flow step; omit for the top level.

index.description: Index in the target list (after removing the moved step). Omit to append.

StepPatch.description:
Partial update of a step. Absent fields are left unchanged; for optional
fields, an explicit `null` clears the value.

params.description: JSON Merge Patch (RFC 7386) applied to `params`: keys set to `null` are removed.

requires.description:
Replaces `requires` (plugin version ranges). Core still adds plugins
that steps use and drops unused ones afterwards.

validation.description:
Full validation of the new revision. Drafts may contain errors;
they must be fixed before the flow can run.

path.description: JSON Pointer into the flow document.

hint.description: How to fix it, written for AI clients (and shown to humans in Studio).

description.description: Description written for both humans and AI clients.

blocks.description: Child blocks allowed on this step (empty for action steps).

hasOutput.description: Whether the step produces a value that `saveAs` can capture.

expressionParams.description: Params whose string value is an expression (not a template).

bindsVariables.description: Params that declare a variable name (introduced into scope).

examples.description:
Complete, valid step objects showing typical use (IDs omitted). AI
clients get them from `get_step_schema` and can copy them.

targets.description:
Params that name a site or a program, checked against the
workspace policy (`policy.json` `sites` / `apps`) before each run of
the step.

secretParams.description:
Params that may take a registered secret,
`{ "secret": "<name>", "field": "password" }`, instead of text.
Secrets are rejected everywhere else.

pathParams.description:
Params that name a file or folder (a string, or a list of strings).
A relative path there is resolved from the flow's folder
(`input/orders.xlsx`). File resources are included automatically.

defaultTimeoutMs.description:
Timeout when the step sets none (takes precedence over the
flow's default), for steps that wait on people (manual login).

deprecated.description:
Set when the type should no longer be used in new steps. It keeps
working; validation warns and points at the replacement.

plugin.description: The plugin that provides this type (`None` for built-in types).

oneOf.description: Web APIs (`http.*`).
Programs, the clipboard and dialogs (`process.*`, `clipboard.*`, `dialog.*`).
Databases through ODBC (`db.*`).

BlockDef.description: Named child block of a control-flow step.

RiskLevel.description: Risk level used by the permission layer (MCP approval, allow-lists).

oneOf.description: No side effects outside the run (variables, logs, control flow).
Interacts with applications or pages (clicks, typing, navigation).
May destroy data or reach outside the machine (file delete, downloads, process kill).

TargetDef.description:
A step param that names something outside the run, checked against the
policy before the step executes.

TargetKind.description: What kind of target a step param names.

oneOf.description: A URL, checked against `sites`.
A program (path or file name), checked against `apps`.

Deprecation.description: Why a step type is deprecated and what to use instead.

note.description: What to do instead, for people and AI clients.

replacement.description: The step type that replaces this one, if any.

PluginInfo.description:
A plugin (an extension, in Studio) that provides step types, as
installed on this PC, with what Studio shows about it.

name.description: The plugin's name, also the prefix of its step types.

label.description: The plugin's display name (its palette group).

tag.description:
Where its nodes work, shown as the tag before a node's name
("AI-OCR"). Empty: the label.

icon.description: A Lucide icon name for its nodes (`scan-text`).

credentials.description:
The registered secrets it takes, by kind, so Studio offers the
right ones (and a form of that kind) for its secret params.

summary.description:
What this step does, in one sentence for people (Studio shows it
under the node's name; `description` is written for AI clients).

external.description:
What this step sends outside the PC, when it does: shown on the
review panel before publishing.

PluginCredential.description: A secret a plugin's steps take: of which kind, and in which params.

label.description: What to register, for people ("Azure のキー").

params.description: The step params (in `secretParams`) that take it.

SecretKind.description:
What a secret holds, so Studio can name its fields and the AI can tell
a login from an API key. Every kind is stored, referenced (`{ "secret",
"field" }`), site-checked and masked the same way: the kind only changes
how the fields are called and which ones a person fills in.

oneOf.description: A user name and password typed into a site or app (and an MFA key).

A fixed key or token for a web API, kept in `password` and sent by
`http.request` (`authType` `bearer` or `header`).

An app registered at an OAuth provider: `username` = client ID,
`password` = client secret. `oauth.signIn` gets the access token.

ExternalUse.description: Data a step sends to a service outside the PC.

service.description: The service it is sent to ("Azure AI Document Intelligence").

data.description: What is sent ("読み取る画像・PDF").

param.description: The param holding the address it is sent to, when it has one.

revision.description: Revision of the flow after this change.

summary.description: The author's own explanation of the change (an AI's `summary`).

checks.description: What the author asked a person to confirm before approving (an AI's `checks`).

stepIds.description: Steps the change added, changed, moved or removed.

Actor.description: Who made a change. Recorded in history and the audit journal.

name.description: Client name, e.g. the MCP client's reported name.

oneOf.description:
An AI in a chat window without MCP (Microsoft Copilot, ...): a
person pasted its answer into Studio. Reviewed like an MCP edit.

ChangeEvent.description: Notification sent to in-process listeners after every committed change.

ErrorPayload.description: Serializable error shape returned over IPC / MCP.

name.description: Short name, e.g. "v1" or "本番リリース".

note.description: What changed or why this version matters.

FlowVersion.description: One named snapshot of a flow.

number.description: Per-flow sequence number (1, 2, …). This is how versions are referenced.

uid.description: Globally unique ID; keeps versions apart when bundles are imported.

revision.description: Flow revision the snapshot was taken from.

VersionSummary.description: Listing entry for versions (no flow body).

identical.description: True when the contents are the same (names, variables, steps, settings).

flow.description:
Flow-level fields: name, description, tags, settings, and each
named part (`parts.<name>`; `before` / `after` is absent when it was
added / removed).

DiffSide.description: Which side of a comparison: a version number, or the current content.

version.description: Version number; absent for the current content.

StepChange.description:
One step-level difference. Added and removed subtrees are reported once,
at their top step (`stepCount` includes the children).

StepLocation.description: Where a step sits: top level (`parentId` absent) or a parent's block.

FlowBundle.description: File format for moving a flow (and its versions) between workspaces.

subflows.description:
Every flow `flow` calls (directly or through others), without
versions, so the bundle runs on its own.

files.description:
Files of the flows' folders (`input/`, `config/`, `templates/`
and the author's own; not `output/`, `work/` or `logs/`).

BundledFile.description: A file carried in a bundle.

flowId.description:
The flow (the bundle's own or one of its sub-flows) whose
folder it belongs to.

ImportOutcome.description: Result of importing a bundle or flow file.

versionsAdded.description: Versions from the bundle that were added (already present ones are skipped).

subflows.description: The bundle's sub-flows and what happened to each.

validation.description:
Full validation of the new revision. Drafts may contain errors;
they must be fixed before the flow can run.

ImportedSubflow.description: One sub-flow of an imported bundle.

SubflowImport.description: What importing a bundle did with one of its sub-flows.

oneOf.description: It was not in the workspace and was added with the same ID.
It existed and was updated (`onConflict: "update"`).
It existed and was left as it is.

PackageManifest.description: What a package holds and what the receiving PC needs.

appVersion.description: Version of SpellSheet that wrote it.

exportedBy.description: Who wrote it (the Windows user name), when known.

contents.description: Every entry other than the manifest.

version.description: The version the content is, if it is one.

published.description: Whether the content is the version published on the PC it came from.

PackageRequires.description: What the flow (and the flows it calls) needs on the PC that runs it.

secrets.description: Names of the logins (secrets) the steps use. Never their values.

sites.description: Sites the steps open (`https://host`), when written out literally.

apps.description: Programs the steps start, when written out literally.

inputs.description: Inputs asked for when the flow runs (no default value).

PackagePlan.description: What exporting would put in, for the export dialog.

hasUnpublishedChanges.description: Whether the current content differs from the published version.

current.description: The plan is for the current content (not the published version).

fileName.description: File name to save as (without folder).

PackageFileChoice.description: A file that may go into a package, for choosing before exporting.

flowName.description: Name of that flow (the main flow or a sub-flow).

includedByDefault.description: Whether it goes in with the default options (`input/` does not).

includeInput.description:
Include files under `input/`. Off by default: they are usually real
business data (and may hold personal data).

only.description:
Exactly these files, when set (`include_input` and `exclude` are then
ignored). A file not listed, such as one of a sub-flow the person did
not see, stays out.

exportedBy.description: Shown to the receiver as who wrote the package.

PackageContent.description: Which content of the flow goes into a package.

oneOf.description: The published version when there is one, otherwise the current content.
The published version (fails when nothing is published).
The current content, also when it is not saved as a version.
Only the version the content is (if any).
Every version of the flow.

FileRef.description: A file of a flow's folder, by flow and path.

PackagePreview.description: What importing a package would do, shown before importing.

ExistingFlow.description: The flow with the same ID that is already in the workspace.

hasPackageVersion.description: The package's version is already here (same `uid`).

diff.description: From the current content here to the package's content.

keptInputs.description:
The package's files under `input/` that an update leaves out,
because this PC already has a file of that name there.

RequirementCheck.description: One thing the package needs, checked against this PC.

name.description: Plugin name, login name, site origin or program.

installed.description: Installed version when it does not match.

CheckStatus.description: State of one requirement on this PC.

oneOf.description: Not installed / not registered here.
Installed at a version outside the range.
The workspace's policy does not allow it.

name.description: What people call it, such as 経理課.

error.description: Why the folder could not be read (not reachable, no access…).

DistributedFlow.description: The newest version of one flow in a folder.

path.description: The file to take it in from.

localVersion.description: Newest version number on this PC, when it has the flow.

DistributedState.description: How a flow in the folder stands against this PC.

oneOf.description: Not on this PC.
This PC has the flow, and the folder has a newer version.
This PC already has that version.
This PC has a newer version than the folder.

ExtractOutcome.description: Result of moving steps into a new sub-flow.

subflow.description: The new flow holding the steps.

caller.description: The calling flow, with the steps replaced by one `flow.call`.

ImportConflict.description: What to do when an imported flow's ID already exists.

oneOf.description:
Apply the imported content to the existing flow (one undoable
edit) and add the bundle's versions that are not there yet.
Import as a new flow with a new ID.

WorkspaceInfo.description: Where a workspace keeps its data, for display and diagnostics.

localRoot.description: Undo history, run records and audit logs of this PC.

ChangeNote.description: What the author of a change says about it (MCP edit tools).

summary.description: Why the change was made, in the author's words. Kept in the journal.

checks.description:
Things the author wants a person to decide or confirm before the change
is approved (assumptions, guesses), one question each. Kept in the journal.

observations.description:
Observations (screens looked at with inspect_* / test_step) the change
is based on. They are linked to the new revision and its steps.

ObservationId.description: Identifier of a screen an AI looked at (review evidence).

ReviewTimeline.description: What to review: the changes since the last approval and their evidence.

sinceRevision.description:
Changes and evidence after this revision are listed (by default the
last approved revision, or 0).

openFeedback.description:
The latest review when it sent the flow back and nobody approved
it since: what the AI still has to address.

evidence.description: Test runs, observations and reviews, oldest first.

oneOf.description: A run an AI started over MCP to test `revision`.

version.description: Named version the run's content matched.

oneOf.description: An observation named by the edit that created `revision`.
An AI saved (or replaced) the test case `name` (`tests/<name>.json`).

description.description: The case's `description` when it was saved: the promise in words.

replaced.description: It replaced a case of the same name.

oneOf.description: An AI ran test cases over MCP against `revision`.

RunId.description: Identifier of a single flow execution.

oneOf.description: The screen when an interactive run in Studio paused on an error.

ReviewVerdict.description: A human's verdict on a revision.

oneOf.description: Sent back to the AI (差し戻し) with a reason.

StepNote.description: A note on one step in a review.

CaseOutcome.description: How one test case went in a `testCases` record.

Mismatch.description:
One difference between what the case expects and what the run did.
`actual` is `null` when the run had no such value.

ChangeRecord.description: One change in a review timeline (a journal entry without its ops).

revision.description: The revision that was reviewed; must still be the current one.

reason.description: Why it was sent back (required for `rejected`) or a remark.

ObservationContent.description: An observation with the contents of its files, for Studio.

treeFile.description: File name of the UI tree (`tree.txt`) in the observation's folder.

notes.description: What was cut or left out to keep the size down.

linked.description: Revisions whose edits named this observation as their basis.

PublishedState.description:
The published version of a flow (what `spellsheet run <id>` and
other unattended runs execute).

revision.description: Revision the version was taken from.

matchesCurrent.description:
Whether the current (working) content equals the published version.
`false` means there are changes that do not run unattended yet.

version.description:
Version to publish. Omitted: the current content, saved as a new
version first unless one already matches it.

name.description: Name of the version created for the current content (default `v<n>`).

expectedRevision.description:
With `version` omitted: fail with REVISION_CONFLICT unless the
current revision is this one (what the person reviewed).

PublishRecord.description:
One line of `versions/<flow-id>/publish.jsonl`: which version runs
unattended from now on (`None`: none, the flow was withdrawn). The
last line is in force; earlier lines are the record of who published
what, kept in the shared part of the workspace.

uid.description: The version's `uid`, so a record never points at another snapshot.

sites.description:
Sites `browser.open`, `http.request` (and plugin steps that declare a
site param) may reach: origins such as `https://order.example.co.jp`,
or `https://*.example.co.jp` for every subdomain. Empty: any site.

apps.description:
Programs `desktop.launch` and `process.run` may start: a full path
(`C:\Program Files\Billing\billing.exe`) or a file name that matches
in any folder (`notepad.exe`). Empty: any program.

flows.description: Per-flow settings, keyed by flow ID.

records.description: How long this PC keeps run records (`runs/`).

remote.description:
Runs asked for by a management server (see
docs/design/remote-runs.md). Off unless enabled here.

notify.description: Who hears about unattended runs (the agent's and `spellsheet run`).

desktop.description: Nodes that use the mouse and keyboard when the screen is locked.

AiPolicy.description:
What an AI client (MCP) may do. Studio and the CLI are people and are not
asked.

runFlow.description:
`run_flow`, by the riskiest step the run may execute (including
the flows it calls).

testStep.description:
`test_step`, by the step's risk (a `flow.call` counts as the
riskiest step of the flows it calls).

ByRisk.description: A decision for each step risk level.

Decision.description: What happens when an AI asks for an action.

oneOf.description: A person approves (or refuses) the exact request in Studio first.

aiRun.description:
Whether an AI may run or test this flow. Overrides `ai.runFlow`
(and `ai.testStep` for calls of it) when it is stricter.

unattended.description:
`false`: `spellsheet run` (scheduled, unattended) refuses it; it only
runs from Studio. Default `true`.

keepDays.description:
Delete run records older than this many days ([`DEFAULT_KEEP_DAYS`]
when left out, `0` keeps them for good).

keepRuns.description: Keep at most this many run records (the newest).

failureScreenshots.description:
When a run fails at a browser or desktop step, keep a picture of that
screen beside the run's log (`logs/<time>_failed.png`). On unless `false`.

manualScreens.description:
When the flow is run from Studio, keep a picture of the screen at
each browser or desktop step (the first time it runs) for the
flow's 手順書. The pictures stay on this PC. On unless `false`.

RemotePolicy.description:
Runs a management server may ask this PC for. Everything is closed by
default; `flows.<id>.unattended: false` still refuses a flow.

enabled.description: Connect to the management server at all.

flows.description: Flow IDs it may start (`"*"` for every flow). Empty: none.

acceptBundles.description:
Run flows the server sends as bundles (not only the published
versions in this workspace).

NotifyRule.description: One place unattended runs are reported to.

on.description: Which endings to report (and `waiting`). Default: failures only.

flows.description: Only these flow IDs (default: every flow).

webhook.description:
The webhook URL (`https://`). Anyone with it can post to the channel:
treat it like a password.

RunOutcome.description: How an unattended run ended, for [`NotifyRule::on`], or that it waits.

oneOf.description:
Not an ending: a step started waiting for a person (a login in the
browser, a dialog). Sent once for each wait, while it waits.

NotifyFormat.description: The shape of the message posted to a webhook.

oneOf.description:
A card for a Microsoft Teams "Workflows" webhook (or Power Automate's
"When a HTTP request is received", which can also send mail).
`{ "text": … }` for a Slack incoming webhook (and many chat tools).
The run's summary as JSON, for your own systems.

DesktopPolicy.description:
What nodes that use the mouse and keyboard do while the screen is
locked (docs/design/locked-runs.md).

waitUnlockedMinutes.description:
Wait up to this many minutes for someone to unlock the screen before
stopping with `DESKTOP_UNAVAILABLE`. Without it (or 0) they stop at
once. For PCs with people at them: the run goes on after lunch.

ApprovalId.description: Identifier of a request for a person's approval of an AI action.

AiAction.description: AI actions the policy can hold for approval.

oneOf.description: Approved and already used by the action.

ProjectFiles.description: What a flow's project folder holds.

folders.description:
Every folder, relative and `/`-separated: the standard ones first,
then the author's own (`input/2026`), sorted.

files.description: Every file except `flow.json`, sorted by path.

ProjectFile.description: One file in a project folder.

path.description:
Relative to the project folder, `/`-separated (`input/orders.xlsx`).
Write it as is in a step's path param.

inUse.description:
Open in Excel or Word (their `~$` owner file is next to it): a run
that writes it fails with `FILE_IN_USE`.

ConfigFile.description:
A settings file (`config/*.json`) kept out of the flow: values a
person changes without touching the flow (a cut-off day, a recipient, a
folder). Studio edits it as a form; `config.read` turns it into
`{ "締め日": 25, … }`.

name.description: The key in the object `config.read` returns (`settings.締め日`).

description.description: What the setting is for, shown under it in the form.

oneOf.description: `yyyy-MM-dd` text.
A list of texts.

description.description: What the case is about, in the author's words.

inputs.description: Values of the flow's input variables, as `spellsheet run -i` takes them.

Expect.description: What should come out of the run.

status.description: How the run ends. `failed` for a case that checks an error is raised.

outputs.description: Output variables to compare (a subset, see the module docs).

errorStep.description: The node the run should stop at, when `status` is `failed`.
